properties.name: Missouri
properties.note: Missouri legislature extended CLARK's boundary line north of the commonly accepted boundary between Missouri and Iowa Territory (the Indian boundary line established in 1816); the extension overlapped Iowa's VAN BUREN.

properties.name: Arkansas
properties.note: Survey of boundary between the Republic of Texas and the United States began. MILLER (original) officially became extinct and LAFAYETTE was eliminated from Texas when Texas claims to the area were upheld.

properties.name: Florida
properties.note: The state of Florida was created from Florida Territory, with boundaries the same as those set in 1822; Florida Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Texas
properties.note: The state of Texas was admitted to the Union; Republic of Texas eliminated.

properties.name: Oregon Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: The Oregon Boundary Treaty between the United States and Great Britain ended joint occupancy of the Oregon Country.

properties.name: District of Columbia
properties.note: The federal government retroceded to Virginia all of the District of Columbia west of the Potomac River, including all of ALEXANDRIA (now ARLINGTON, Va.). ALEXANDRIA eliminated from the District of Columbia.

properties.name: Virginia
properties.note: The District of Columbia ceded ALEXANDRIA (now ARLINGTON) to Virginia.

properties.name: Iowa
properties.note: The state of Iowa was created from Iowa Territory; Iowa Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: The state of Iowa was created from Iowa Territory. All of the former Territory north and west of the present state became unorganized federal territory.

properties.name: Wisconsin
properties.note: The state of Wisconsin was created from Wisconsin Territory. The area in present Minnesota between the Mississippi River and the state of Wisconsin continued as de facto Wisconsin Territory until the creation of Minnesota Territory on 3 March 1849.

properties.name: Wisconsin Territory De Facto
properties.note: The state of Wisconsin was created from Wisconsin Territory. The area in present Minnesota between the Mississippi River and the state of Wisconsin continued as de facto Wisconsin Territory until the creation of Minnesota Territory on 3 March 1849.

properties.name: Mexican Cession
properties.note: Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo ended the war between Mexico and the United States. Area ceded by Mexico became Unorganized Federal Territory (non-county area) in the United States.

properties.name: Oregon Territory
properties.note: The United States created the Territory of Oregon, encompassing all of present Oregon, Washington, and Idaho, and parts of present Montana and Wyoming.

properties.name: Missouri
properties.note: U.S. Supreme Court settled boundary dispute between Iowa and Missouri by rejecting both states' claims, choosing instead the commonly accepted boundary before the dispute arose and the present boundary between the two states.

properties.name: Minnesota Territory
properties.note: The United States created Minnesota Territory from unorganized federal territory west of the Mississippi River (formerly part of Iowa Territory) and de facto Wisconsin Territory.

properties.name: Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: Unorganized federal territory lost to creation of Minnesota Territory; all of present North and South Dakota west of the Missouri and White Earth Rivers remained unorganized federal territory.

properties.name: Deseret
properties.note: The General Assembly of the newly proposed state of Deseret met on 2 Jul 1849. The state was to include almost all of Utah and parts of present Ariz., Cal., Colo., Ida., Nev., N.Mex., Ore., and Wyo., but proposal never gained support in U.S. Congress.

properties.name: California
properties.note: The state of California was admitted to the Union.

properties.name: Mexican Cession
properties.note: The United States created Utah Territory from the territory ceded by Mexico in the Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo (1848), from territory to be purchased from the state of Texas in December 1850, and from unorganized federal territory.

properties.name: Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: Unorganized federal territory lost to creation of Utah Territory.

properties.name: Utah Territory
properties.note: The United States created Utah Territory from the territory ceded by Mexico in the Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo (1848), from territory to be purchased from the state of Texas in December 1850, and from unorganized federal territory.

properties.name: New Mexico Territory
properties.note: The United States created New Mexico Territory from Unorganized Federal Territory (land ceded by Mexico to the United States in the Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo) and from territory purchased from the state of Texas.

properties.name: Texas
properties.note: State of Texas sold land in present Colorado, Kansas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Wyoming to the United States.

properties.name: Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: The state of Texas sold land in present Kansas, Colorado, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Wyoming to the United States.

properties.name: Oregon Territory
properties.note: The United States created Washington Territory from Oregon Territory.

properties.name: Washington Territory
properties.note: The United States created Washington Territory from Oregon Territory; included all of present Washington and parts of present Idaho and Montana.

properties.name: Gadsden Purchase
properties.note: Gadsden Purchase settled the boundary dispute between the United States and Mexico and established the international line at its present location.

properties.name: Kansas Territory
properties.note: The United States created Kansas Territory from unorganized federal territory; included all of present Kansas and part of present Colorado.

properties.name: Nebraska Territory
properties.note: The United States created Nebraska Territory from unorganized federal territory. Nebraska Territory included all of present Nebraska and parts of present Colorado, Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wyoming.

properties.name: Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: The United States created Kansas Territory and Nebraska Territory from unorganized federal territory.

properties.name: New Mexico Territory
properties.note: The territory acquired by the United States in the Gadsden Purchase was officially added to New Mexico Territory.

properties.name: Massachusetts
properties.note: New York acquired the southwestern corner of Massachusetts, known as Boston Corner.

properties.name: New York
properties.note: New York acquired the southwestern corner of Massachusetts (Boston Corner).

properties.name: Minnesota
properties.note: The state of Minnesota was created from Minnesota Territory;  Minnesota Territory eliminated. The remainder of Minnesota Territory (west of the present state boundary) became unorganized federal territory.

properties.name: Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: The state of Minnesota was created from Minnesota Territory; Minnesota Territory eliminated. That part of present North and South Dakota east of the Missouri and White Earth Rivers became unorganized federal territory.

properties.name: Oregon
properties.note: The state of Oregon was created from Oregon Territory; Oregon Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Washington Territory
properties.note: Washington Territory gained non-county area when the state of Oregon was created from Oregon Territory. Non-County Area 2 included parts of present Idaho, Montana, and Wyoming.

properties.name: Kentucky
properties.note: ROBERTSON (Tenn.) and SUMNER (Tenn.) gained from SIMPSON (Ky.) when surveyors re-marking the Kentucky-Tennessee boundary acted without authority and shifted the line around two small parcels.

properties.name: Tennessee
properties.note: ROBERTSON (Tenn.) and SUMNER (Tenn.) gained from SIMPSON (Ky.) when surveyors remarking the Kentucky-Tennessee boundary acted without authority and shifted the line around two small parcels.

properties.name: Kansas
properties.note: The state of Kansas was created from Kansas Territory; Kansas Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: Area within present Colorado that had been part of Kansas Terr. temporarily reverted to unorganized federal territory until official creation of Colorado Terr. on 28 Feb 1861. State of Kansas was admitted to the union this date; Kansas Terr. eliminated.

properties.name: Colorado Territory
properties.note: The United States created Colorado Territory from Nebraska, New Mexico, and Utah Territories, and from the former Kansas Territory.

properties.name: Nebraska Territory
properties.note: Nebraska Territory lost to creation of Colorado Territory; Nebraska Territory included all of present Nebraska and parts of present Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wyoming.

properties.name: New Mexico Territory
properties.note: The United States created Colorado Territory from New Mexico, Utah, Kansas, and Nebraska Territories.

properties.name: Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: The United States created Colorado Territory from Nebraska, New Mexico, and Utah Territories, and from the former Kansas Territory. Boundaries were identical to the state of Colorado.

properties.name: Utah Territory
properties.note: The United States created Colorado Territory from Nebraska, New Mexico, and Utah Territories, and from the former Kansas Territory.

properties.name: Dakota Territory
properties.note: The United States created Dakota Territory from Nebraska Territory and unorganized federal territory; included all of present North Dakota, South Dakota, and parts of present Montana, Nebraska and Wyoming.

properties.name: Nebraska Territory
properties.note: Nebraska Territory gained from Utah and Washington Territories, lost to creation of Dakota Territory. Nebraska Territory included most of present Nebraska and part of Wyoming.

properties.name: Nevada Territory
properties.note: The United States created Nevada Territory from Utah Territory.

properties.name: Unorganized Federal Territory
properties.note: The United States created Dakota Territory from Nebraska Territory and Unorganized Federal Territory.

properties.name: Utah Territory
properties.note: The United States created Nevada Territory from Utah Territory. Utah Territory also lost to Nebraska Territory when Nebraska Territory gained area in present Wyoming from Utah Territory.

properties.name: Washington Territory
properties.note: Nebraska Territory gained part of SHOSHONE (Idaho).

properties.name: Massachusetts
properties.note: BRISTOL gained from NEWPORT (R.I.) and lost to PROVIDENCE (R.I.) when Massachusetts and Rhode Island implemented the U.S. Supreme Court settlement (31 December 1861) of their boundary to the Atlantic Ocean.

properties.name: Rhode Island
properties.note: NEWPORT lost to BRISTOL (Mass.) and PROVIDENCE gained from BRISTOL (Mass.) when Massachusetts and Rhode Island implemented the U. S. Supreme Court settlement (31 December 1861) of their boundary to the Atlantic Ocean.

properties.name: Nevada Territory
properties.note: Nevada Territory gained from Utah Territory.

properties.name: Utah Territory
properties.note: Nevada Territory gained from Utah Territory.

properties.name: Arizona Territory
properties.note: The United States created  Arizona Territory from the western portion of New Mexico Territory and a part of present Nevada.

properties.name: New Mexico Territory
properties.note: The United States created Arizona Territory from New Mexico Territory.

properties.name: Dakota Territory
properties.note: The United States created Idaho Territory from Dakota, Nebraska, and Washington Territories. Dakota Territory was reduced to the area of present North Dakota and South Dakota, plus a small area of present Nebraska.

properties.name: Idaho Territory
properties.note: The United States created Idaho Territory from Dakota, Nebraska, and Washington Territories.

properties.name: Nebraska Territory
properties.note: Nebraska Territory lost the area in present Wyoming to creation of Idaho Territory.

properties.name: Washington Territory
properties.note: The United States created Idaho Territory from Dakota, Nebraska, and Washington Territories.

properties.name: Virginia
properties.note: The state of West Virginia was formally separated from Virginia and admitted to the Union. Most of West Virginia had been effectively independent of Virginia since June 1861.

properties.name: West Virginia
properties.note: The state of West Virginia was formally separated from Virginia and admitted to the Union. Most of West Virginia had been effectively independent of Virginia since June 1861.

properties.name: Virginia
properties.note: Virginia lost BERKELEY (W.Va.) to West Virginia.

properties.name: West Virginia
properties.note: BERKELEY was separated from Virginia and became a county in the state of West Virginia.

properties.name: Virginia
properties.note: The state of Virginia lost JEFFERSON (W.Va.) to West Virginia.

properties.name: West Virginia
properties.note: JEFFERSON was separated from Virginia and became a county in the state of West Virginia.

properties.name: Dakota Territory
properties.note: Dakota Territory gained from Idaho Territory; included most of present Wyoming and a small area of about two square miles in present Montana that had been part of MADISON (Mont.).

properties.name: Idaho Territory
properties.note: The United States created Montana Territory from Idaho Territory with boundaries identical to the state of Montana; Dakota Territory gained most of present Wyoming from Idaho Territory.

properties.name: Montana Territory
properties.note: The United States created Montana Territory from Idaho Territory; boundaries were identical to the state of Montana, except for a small area of about two square miles (formerly part of MADISON) that became part of Dakota Territory.

properties.name: Nevada
properties.note: The state of Nevada was created from Nevada Territory and admitted to the Union by presidential proclamation.

properties.name: Arizona Territory
properties.note: State of Nevada gained parts of MOHAVE and PAH-UTE (extinct) when the United States transferred the portion of Arizona Territory lying between 37 degrees and 42 degrees of north latitude and west of 114 degrees west longitude to Nevada.

properties.name: Nevada
properties.note: Nevada Territory gained from Utah Territory and from Arizona Territory.

properties.name: Utah Territory
properties.note: The state of Nevada gained from Utah Territory.

properties.name: Nebraska
properties.note: The state of Nebraska was created from Nebraska Territory; Nebraska Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Alaska Department
properties.note: The United States acquired Alaska from Russia. Presidential proclamation issued 20 June 1867. Alaska was considered an "unorganized territory" with no organized civil government.

properties.name: Dakota Territory
properties.note: The small remnant of Dakota Territory in present Montana again became non-county area when Wyoming Territory boundaries were established.

properties.name: Idaho Territory
properties.note: The United States created Wyoming Territory from Dakota, Idaho, and Utah Territories, and from part of ONEIDA.

properties.name: Utah Territory
properties.note: The United States created Wyoming Territory from Dakota, Idaho, and Utah Territories.

properties.name: Wyoming Territory
properties.note: The United States created Wyoming Territory with present boundaries from Dakota, Idaho, and Utah Territories.

properties.name: Dakota Territory
properties.note: UNION lost small area to the state of Nebraska when the Missouri River changed course.

properties.name: Nebraska
properties.note: DAKOTA gained small area from UNION (S.D.) in Dakota Territory when the Missouri River changed course.

properties.name: Dakota Territory
properties.note: TRIPP created by Dakota Territory in present South Dakota from GREGORY, TODD (original, extinct), and Non-County Area (1); TRIPP included a small piece of present Nebraska.

properties.name: Nebraska
properties.note: TRIPP created by Dakota Territory in present South Dakota from GREGORY, TODD (original, extinct), and Non-County Area (1); TRIPP included a small piece of present Nebraska.

properties.name: Dakota Territory
properties.note: Montana Territory gained the small remnant of Dakota Territory that remained between Montana and Wyoming Territories.

properties.name: Montana Territory
properties.note: Montana Territory gained the small remnant of Dakota Territory that remained between Montana and Wyoming Territories.

properties.name: Colorado
properties.note: The state of Colorado was created from Colorado Territory; Colorado Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Dakota Territory
properties.note: GREGORY, TRIPP, and TODD (original, extinct) each lost to the state of Nebraska. TODD implicitly gained part of Fort Randall Military Reserve, and the remaining part of the Military Reserve became part of the state of Nebraska.

properties.name: Nebraska
properties.note: The state of Nebraska gained the area between 43 degrees north latitude and the Keya Paha and Niobrara Rivers from Dakota Territory. This territory became Non-County Area 8 in Nebraska.

properties.name: Alaska District
properties.note: The United States Congress established a civil government for Alaska. This act was limited and resulted in a partial organization of Alaska as a territory.

properties.name: North Dakota
properties.note: The state of North Dakota was created from the Dakota Territory; Dakota Territory eliminated.

properties.name: South Dakota
properties.note: The state of South Dakota was created from the Dakota Territory; Dakota Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Montana
properties.note: The state of Montana created from Montana Territory and to the Union by Presidential proclamation; Montana Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Washington
properties.note: The state of Washington was created from Washington Territory; Washington Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Indian Territory
properties.note: The United States created Oklahoma Territory from Indian Territory and unorganized federal territory (the Oklahoma panhandle or Public Land Strip).

properties.name: Oklahoma Territory
properties.note: The United States created Oklahoma Territory from Indian Territory and unorganized federal territory (the Oklahoma panhandle or Public Land Strip).

properties.name: Idaho
properties.note: The state of Idaho was created from Idaho Territory; Idaho Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Wyoming
properties.note: The state of Wyoming was created from Wyoming Territory; Wyoming Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Provisional Government of Hawaii
properties.note: Part of the present-day US not covered by any jurisdiction drawn for this period; label = colonial power by date for this acquisition region.

properties.name: Indian Territory
properties.note: Oklahoma Territory gained a portion of the Indian Territory, designated the Cherokee Outlet, under a treaty between the United States and the Cherokee Nation.

properties.name: Oklahoma Territory
properties.note: Oklahoma Territory gained a portion of the Indian Territory, designated the Cherokee Outlet, under a treaty between the United States and the Cherokee Nation.

properties.name: Republic of Hawaii
properties.note: Part of the present-day US not covered by any jurisdiction drawn for this period; label = colonial power by date for this acquisition region.

properties.name: Utah
properties.note: The state of Utah was created from Utah Territory; Utah Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Texas
properties.note: GREER eliminated from Texas when U.S. Supreme Court ruled that GREER was not within the boundaries of Texas, but was under the jurisdiction of the United States. GREER became a county in Oklahoma Territory on 4 May 1896.

properties.name: Hawaii Annexation
properties.note: President McKinley signed a joint resolution of Congress annexing Hawaii to the United States.

properties.name: Hawaii Territory
properties.note: The United States created the Territory of Hawaii.

properties.name: Nebraska
properties.note: CLAY (S.D.) officially gained an island in the Missouri River from DIXON (Neb.); voters approved the gain 1006 to 25.

properties.name: South Dakota
properties.note: CLAY (S.D.) officially gained an island in the Missouri River from DIXON (Neb.); voters approved the gain 1006 to 25.

properties.name: Oklahoma
properties.note: The state of Oklahoma was created from Oklahoma Territory and Indian Territory; Oklahoma Territory and Indian Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Michigan
properties.note: The new Michigan constitution redefined part of the interstate boundary with Wisconsin across the Upper Peninsula. GOGEBIC (Mich.) implicitly overlapped Wisconsin (IRON and VILAS Counties), but Wisconsin kept control of the disputed area.

properties.name: New Mexico
properties.note: The state of New Mexico was created from New Mexico Territory; New Mexico Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Arizona
properties.note: The state of Arizona was created from Arizona Territory; Arizona Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Alaska Territory
properties.note: Alaska was fully organized as a territory in the United States.

properties.name: Michigan
properties.note: Michigan took its 1909 boundary dispute with Wisconsin to the United States Supreme Court and expanded its scope by claiming more territory on the Upper Peninsula and more of the waters and islands of Green Bay.

properties.name: Michigan
properties.note: The United States Supreme Court decided the dispute between Michigan and Wisconsin entirely in favor of Wisconsin; implicit overlaps of Wisconsin by DELTA, GOGEBIC, and IRON ended.

properties.name: Wisconsin
properties.note: An overlap was created when Wisconsin appeared to gain islands north of the Rock Island Passage from Michigan when the U.S. Supreme Court described the Wis.-Mich. boundary through Lake Michigan and Green Bay and introduced some unintentional errors.

properties.name: Wisconsin
properties.note: Dispute between Michigan and Wisconsin ended when the U.S. Supreme Court decreed the precise course of the revised Michigan-Wisconsin boundary through Green Bay and Lake Michigan.

properties.name: Kansas
properties.note: Missouri and Kansas exchanged territory along the Missouri River from 40 degrees north latitude to the Kansas River. The change was made to accommodate shifts in the course of the Missouri River following the 1944 flood.

properties.name: Missouri
properties.note: Missouri and Kansas exchanged territory along the Missouri River from 40 degrees north latitude to the Kansas River. The change was made to accommodate shifts in the course of the Missouri River following the 1944 flood.

properties.name: Alaska
properties.note: The state of Alaska was created from Alaska Territory by Presidential proclamation; Alaska Territory eliminated.

properties.name: Hawaii
properties.note: The state of Hawaii was created from Hawaii Territory; Hawaii Territory eliminated.

properties.name: California
properties.note: Between 1949 and 1959 (precise date unknown) SAN FRANCISCO gained a small area of the Alameda Naval Air Station when landfill expansion extended westward over the county line between SAN FRANCISCO and ALAMEDA in San Francisco Bay.
